body.p: Claims 1-26 were previously pending with Claims 1, 12, and 23 being independent. Claims 1, 12, and 23 have been amended herein. Support for the amendments can be found at the least at

Claims 1-5, 7, 12-16, and 23-25 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0245910 to Mallas et al. ("Mallas") and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0167,167 to Mitchell ("Mitchell"). Claims 6 and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell and in further view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2002/0042561 to Schulman et al. ("Schulman"). Claims 8-11, 19-22, and 26 stand rejected as allegedly being obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0270,617 to Muller ("Muller"). As a prima facie case of the obviousness of claims 1-26 cannot be established based upon the asserted combination of references, Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections as set forth below.
Applicant submits that the claims, as amended with the proposed amendments, are allowable over the cited art.

Claim 1 is amended to recite subject matter directed to the working electrode voltage source, the counter electrode voltage source, and the guard ring voltage source being separate voltage sources. Support for the amendments can be found at least at [0040] - [0044] and FIG.

[0032]; FIG. 4A. Fennell requires that the guard electrode and working electrode maintain the same voltage. Fennell at [0032]. Fennell is silent with respect to using separate voltage sources for the working electrode, the counter electrode, and the guard electrode. The instant claims, as amended, use separate voltage sources for each of these elements allowing the voltage for each to be varied from the others. Accordingly, Fennell cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims, as amended.

Mallas fails to cure the deficiencies of Fennell. Mallas describes using a singular voltage source connected to an operational amplifier to provide power to both the working electrode and the counter electrode. Mallas at [0220]; FIG. 8A. Mallas describes that "the voltage generation or application device 810 supplies a voltage, e.g., the first voltage or the second voltage, to an input terminal of an operational amplifier 840." Mallas at [0220]. As such, "voltage from the voltage generation or application device 810 to the operational amplifier 840 drives a voltage measured at the counter electrode 365." Mallas at [0220]. Mallas also describes that "[t]he voltage generation or application device 810 may also supply the voltage to a working electrode 375 of the sensor 355." Mallas at [0220]. Further, Mallas is silent with respect to the use of a guard ring. Accordingly, Mallas cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims, as amended.

Furthermore, Schulman, Mitchell, and Muller fail to resolve the deficiencies of Fennell and Mallas. Independent claims 12 and 23 have been amended with similar subject matter. For at least the reasons described above, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections of the claims.

Applicant respectfully submits that those dependent claims not discussed separately herein are allowable at least for the reasons discussed with respect to the corresponding independent claims, and respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections thereof be withdrawn.

Applicant submits that claims 1-26, as amended, are in allowable condition and request a corresponding Notice of Allowance. In the event of any outstanding issues, Applicants respectfully request an Examiner Interview to expedite prosecution. Any additional fee that might be due in connection with this application should be applied against Deposit Account No. 50-6159.
